# REGIME READ — 2026-09-03

**[FULL-DATA READ]** WebSearch is available and the option-chain block is present. All seven lenses have live inputs for the third consecutive run, and this run **Lens 1 has a fresh input for the first time in the series** (AAII week ending 2026-09-02, retrieved directly from aaii.com).

**The tape was green and the volatility complex calmed down. The underlying setup got worse.** That is the whole report in two sentences. On 2026-09-02 every major index rose, the 10-year Treasury yield paused after a five-session run to multi-year highs, and four of five options-market fear gauges retreated. Meanwhile **Brent crude ran to $97.25 — now only 2.83% from the $100 level I published as a bearish trigger — gold reversed and rallied 2.56%, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on 700+ US goods were confirmed live for 2026-09-08 (inside the trading window), and Broadcom guided the December quarter below consensus after the close, sending the stock down ~5% after hours.**

**One correction to carry forward, and it is not mine.** A search result titled *"Odds of Fed Rate Hike This Year Fall as Goldman Sachs Warns Against Hawkish Bets"* appears current and puts September hike odds at **30%** — which would have fired my published bullish trigger. I fetched the article: **it is dated 2026-08-17, eleven days before Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.** It is pre-repricing and must not be used. Current odds are ~56–66%, discussed below.

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 (Neutral/choppy) → 3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged for a sixth consecutive read. Last read I held Stage 3 while noting it was strained. **This run the hold is comfortable rather than strained:** VIX fell to **15.34** and VXN fell **4.05%** to **21.07**, so the stage-4 volatility condition moved *away*, not closer.
- **Total score: −6 → −7 (delta −1).** Only one lens moved: **Lens 5 Cross-asset −1 → −2** on Brent's run toward $100 and gold's reversal into a hedge bid. Every other lens held. **Still no positive lens, for the second consecutive read.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bearish (already FIRED last read) — second sub-50DMA close plus a break of $70.00:* **STILL IN FORCE.** TQQQ closed **$69.60**, a **third** consecutive close below the 50-day moving average (**$71.60**, spot −2.80%), and still **$0.40 (0.57%) below $70.00**. The green day did not reclaim either level.
  - *Bullish — TQQQ reclaims $70.00 then closes above the 50DMA:* **ARMED — the closest it has been.** $0.40 from $70.00 (was $0.85); 2.87% from the 50DMA (was 3.55%).
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN < 19:* **ARMED, both legs gained ground.** NDX **29,143.33** is **2.94%** short (was 3.18%); VXN **21.07** is **2.07** points above 19 (was 2.96 above).
  - *Bullish — September hike odds below 40% on CME FedWatch:* **ARMED, moved toward it but nowhere near.** Odds have eased from the 66–68% peak to roughly **56–66%** (CME FedWatch fed funds futures ~56%; Kalshi ~61%; the dated 2026-08-31 Forbes reading was 66%). **I could not pin a single dated 2026-09-03 CME print**, so I report the range rather than a point. Either way, well above 40%.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ loses the 4-week low $67.93:* **ARMED, and it held with more room.** Spot is **+2.40%** above it (was +1.80%).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **ARMED.** NDX must fall **2.55%** (was 2.33% on the same basis — last read printed 2.38% using the other denominator; recomputed here for comparability).
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25:* **ARMED and RECEDED.** 21.07, down from 21.96. Needs +18.7% to trigger.
  - *Bearish — VIX/VIX3M term ratio ≥ 1.00:* **ARMED and RECEDED.** **0.857**, down from 0.891. Note the series: 0.851 → 0.891 → 0.857. Most of last read's flattening was given back, but not all.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25%:* **CLEARED, and drifting wider for a third consecutive run.** **2.65%** (2.60 → 2.63 → 2.65). Still historically very tight.
  - *Bearish — Brent decisively above $100:* **ARMED, and now the nearest trigger of any on the board.** Brent **$97.25**, needing just **+2.83%** — versus +6.25% last read. It has risen **3.33% in one day and 6.4% across three sessions.**
  - *Neutralizer — NFP with an inverted sign:* **PENDING, now one session away (Friday 2026-09-04).**
- **Notable lens flips:** **Lens 5 Cross-asset −1 → −2.** Lens 2 Dealer flow **held at 0 despite a broad improvement** — reasoning in the scorecard. Lenses 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 unchanged at 0, −2, −1, 0, −2.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy.** VIX **15.34** sits comfortably inside the 15–22 band and **fell 6.2% from yesterday's close**. Stage 4 requires VIX 20–30 *and rising* — it is neither. The Nasdaq gauge, VXN at **21.07**, also fell 4.05%. **None of the five Stage-4 triggers has fired, and three of them (VXN > 25, term ratio ≥ 1.00, NDX < 28,400) moved further away this session.** The breadth-deterioration half of the Stage-4 description remains partially satisfied through NDX's persistent underperformance, but the volatility half is not close.
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which reaffirmed the 2% inflation target against price pressures the Fed itself calls elevated and roughly doubled market-implied September hike odds from ~36% to ~66%. The **US–Iran escalation** (conflict phase from 2026-02-28; sharp re-escalation from 2026-08-30) is the amplifier.
- **Position:** Week 1–2 of a combined rate-repricing and geopolitical-escalation leg, inside a Stage-3 range now confirmed across six consecutive reads (08-28, 08-29, 08-31, 09-01, 09-02, 09-03).
- **Confidence:** **Medium.** Four lenses bearish (Macro, Breadth, Cross-asset, Geopolitical), three neutral, **none bullish**. Four aligned lenses = Medium under the scoring rule.
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ 30,000 (+2.94%) **with** VXN < 19 (−9.8%) — or, as the realistic first step, **September hike odds falling below 40% on CME FedWatch** from the current ~56–66%.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above 20 (+30% from 15.34); **or** VXN > 25 (+18.7%); **or** NDX < 28,400 (−2.55%); **or** HY OAS widening through 3.25% from 2.65%; **or** the VIX/VIX3M term ratio rising through 1.00 from 0.857.

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range in which the *price* of risk eased this session — volatility gauges down, yields paused, all indices green — while the *sources* of risk intensified: crude within 2.83% of $100, a hedge bid returning to gold, Canadian retaliatory tariffs landing inside the trading window, and a Fed still leaning toward a hike, at **Medium** confidence.

## Diverging Signals

**The central tension this run is that the market's fear gauges fell while the things worth fearing got closer.** VIX −6.2%, VXN −4.05%, VVIX −5.48%, SKEW off its high, put/call from 1.11 to 0.74, term structure re-steepening — that is a broad, coherent stand-down in the price of protection. In the same 24 hours Brent closed 2.83% from $100, gold reversed into a 2.56% hedge rally, a tanker attack killed two sailors, Canada's tariffs got a hard date inside the window, and the Fed's own Beige Book documented tariff- and energy-driven input inflation. **When protection cheapens into an unimproved setup, the cheapening is the risk, not the reassurance.**

**Second: bond volatility is the dissenter, and it is the one that matters here.** MOVE rose for a third consecutive session, to 79.71. Every equity-side gauge fell. The regime's driver is the rate path, and the gauge that measures rate-path uncertainty has not calmed. That is why Lens 2 stayed at 0 rather than recovering to +1.

**Third: the news daemon improved substantially, and still mis-weighted.** Last read it printed **CLEAR / 0.0** during a military escalation — the worst possible reading. This read it prints **CAUTION / 8.5**, and its signal list now correctly includes **the Strait of Hormuz** (Trump Truth Social, impact 4.0) and **the Fed Beige Book on energy and tariff costs** (impact 4.0). Both blind spots I flagged are now covered. **But its highest-weighted signal at 8.5 is a fashion-industry column about the Canada–US trade war** — a keyword match on "tariff/trade war," not a market-moving event; the underlying tariff news broke on 2026-08-22. **And it missed Broadcom entirely**, which is the single most likely mover of NDX at today's open. The header carries **`news_shock_score: 6`** on my own assessment, not the daemon's 8.5. Coverage fixed; magnitude still unreliable.

**Fourth: today's actual gap risk is a single stock.** **Broadcom reported after the close on 2026-09-02: revenue $29.59bn (+86%) versus $29.36bn expected, adjusted EPS $3.32 versus $3.24 — a clean beat — but guided fiscal Q4 revenue to $34.8bn against $35.03bn expected, and the stock fell ~5% after hours.** AVGO is a top-five NDX constituent. A ~5% move in it is worth roughly a quarter-point of NDX directly, before any semiconductor sympathy move. **This lands on today's session and is not in any number in the tables above.**

**Fifth: TQQQ tracked cleanly again.** TQQQ **+0.65%** against NDX **+0.23%** is a ratio of **2.83×** — within rounding of the fund's 3× design on a small move. Second consecutive clean reconciliation, so the anomaly flagged two reads ago is now closed as a one-off artefact.

**Expected move, from the real quote:** $69.60 × 0.520 × 0.141 = **±$5.10 = ±7.33%**, band **$64.50 – $74.70**. The band narrowed from ±7.9% last read purely because quoted implied volatility fell 4 points. Series note on the `3 × VXN` heuristic: it gives 63.2% against a quoted 52.0%, **21.6% hot** — the widest overshoot of the series (~17% → 10.1% → 17.7% → **21.6%**). The heuristic is consistently and increasingly biased wide; **use the quote wherever it exists.**

**On RSI — one of two consecutive readings must be wrong, and the error sits exactly on a state boundary.** RSI(14) is reported at **29.6** today after **36.8** yesterday, on a day TQQQ rose **+0.65%**. Standard Wilder RSI cannot do that. On any up day, the new gain adds to average gain while average loss decays by a fixed factor, so the ratio — and therefore RSI — must **rise**. A +0.65% day should have taken 36.8 to roughly 37–38, not to 29.6. I cannot determine from the data at hand which of the two prints is correct. **The consequence is not cosmetic: 29.6 is below the 30 line and 36.8 is well above it, so the two readings disagree about whether TQQQ is *oversold* — a distinct state with distinct implications for a put seller.** I am therefore reporting the number as supplied and **declining to call the instrument oversold on the strength of it.**

**On IV/HV — partially rehabilitated from last read, still not fully verified.** IV/HV prints **1.35** (ATM IV 52.0% / HV20 38.2%), above the **1.25** "favourable premium" threshold I published. Last read I refused to bank a 1.44 reading because HV20 had fallen 15.5 points in a single session on a −3.85% day, which the arithmetic does not naturally permit. **This run HV20 moved only 39.0% → 38.2%, a −0.8pp change that is entirely normal.** So the *change* is now credible. But the *level* still descends from that unexplained one-session drop, so the ratio inherits an unverified base. **Treat 1.35 as directionally real — implied volatility is running above recent realized — but not as a precisely trustworthy number.**

## TQQQ Read

- **Momentum: at the oversold boundary, but I am not calling it oversold.** The supplied RSI(14) of **29.6** would place TQQQ below the 30 line for the first time in the series — the condition that, when it comes with stabilising price, tends to pair richer premium with a mean-reversion tailwind. **But as set out above, that reading cannot be reconciled with a +0.65% day following a 36.8 print, and the two candidate values sit on opposite sides of the boundary.** What *is* independently observable: price rose, the down-day streak is broken at **0 red / 1 green**, and the 4-week low held. That is stabilisation, and it is the honest version of the claim. It is not a verified oversold signal.

- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS — both tests measured, both fail, and the margin improved this run.** **DOWNTURN fails on both legs:** spot is **10.65% below** the 4-week high of $77.90 (needs >20%), and **VXN at 21.07 is below the ≥25 requirement** — and moved further below it. **RALLY fails badly:** spot is **2.40% above** the 4-week low of $67.93 (69.60 / 67.93 − 1), against >30% required. So **SIDEWAYS**.
